atomicity.reason: One obligation - a single bound on the first published value after a power cycle.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained - it names both compared values, the bound and its unit.

feasibility.reason: Feasible via a shutdown store, but it collides with REQ_SOC_REST_CORRECTION: a standstill long enough to power-cycle a vehicle also satisfies that requirement's 30-minutes-below-1 A rest condition, and its correction is unbounded in magnitude, so it can legitimately shift the value by more than the 2 % allowed here. Neither requirement states which wins.
feasibility.suggestion: State the precedence explicitly - e.g. exempt the first publication after an open-circuit-voltage correction from this bound, or rate-limit the correction so it cannot breach it.

parent_fit.reason: Directly delivers the parent story's observable that the level does not jump when the vehicle is switched off and on again.

unambiguity.reason: One reading: compare the first post-power-cycle value against the last pre-shutdown value, bounded in percent of rated capacity.

verifiability.reason: The 2 % bound and the observation point (first publication after the power cycle) are concrete, but 'a power cycle in which no charge left or entered the pack' cannot be realised literally - quiescent load and self-discharge always move some charge - so the test precondition is unbounded and the tester must invent one.
verifiability.suggestion: Bound the precondition, e.g. an off period of at most a stated duration with no external charge or discharge and at most a stated charge movement.

summary: Matches the parent's no-jump observable, but its precondition ('no charge left or entered the pack') is not physically realisable as written, and the 2 % bound collides with the unbounded open-circuit-voltage correction, which triggers in exactly the same standstill.
